objetivos.titulo: Photosynthesis: stages and where they occur
objetivos.leitura: Photosynthesis takes place in the chloroplast and has two stages. During the light-dependent reactions, in the thylakoids, light splits water (photolysis), releasing oxygen and producing ATP and NADPH. In the Calvin cycle, in the stroma, that ATP and NADPH are used to fix carbon dioxide and make glucose.
objetivos.vida_real: Think of a bakery with two shifts. The first shift (light-dependent reactions) only works with the lights on and charges the batteries (ATP and NADPH). The second shift (Calvin cycle) uses those batteries to make bread (glucose) with flour from the air (carbon dioxide).
pegadinhas: The oxygen released comes from water, not carbon dioxide.
The Calvin cycle does not use light directly, but it stops without the products of the light-dependent reactions.

questoes.pergunta: In which part of the chloroplast do the light-dependent reactions occur?
questoes.explicacao: The light-dependent reactions take place in the thylakoid membranes; the stroma is where the Calvin cycle takes place.
questoes.trecho: take place in the membranes of the thylakoids

questoes.pergunta: Where does the oxygen released during photosynthesis come from?
questoes.explicacao: Photolysis splits water and releases the oxygen.
questoes.trecho: The oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from water, not carbon dioxide

questoes.pergunta: What does the Calvin cycle use to fix carbon dioxide?
questoes.resposta: The ATP and NADPH from the light-dependent reactions
questoes.explicacao: The 'batteries' from the first stage power the second.
questoes.trecho: It uses the ATP and NADPH from the light-dependent reactions to fix carbon dioxide

objetivos.leitura: Aerobic respiration breaks down glucose to make ATP. Glycolysis, in the cytoplasm, turns one glucose molecule into two pyruvate molecules and does not require oxygen. The Krebs cycle, in the mitochondrial matrix, releases carbon dioxide. The electron transport chain, in the inner mitochondrial membrane, uses oxygen as the final acceptor, forms water, and produces most of the ATP.
objetivos.vida_real: It is like a car: glycolysis is starting the engine (low cost, low output), the Krebs cycle is the engine releasing gas through the exhaust (carbon dioxide), and the electron transport chain is the open road, where the car really performs, but only with oxygen.
pegadinhas: Plants also respire, day and night.

questoes.explicacao: It is the only stage outside the mitochondrion.

questoes.pergunta: What is the final electron acceptor in the electron transport chain?
questoes.explicacao: Oxygen receives the electrons at the end of the chain and forms water.
questoes.trecho: Oxygen is the final electron acceptor and forms water

questoes.pergunta: True or false: plants only respire at night.
questoes.explicacao: They respire day and night; during the day, photosynthesis just makes it less noticeable.
questoes.trecho: plants also carry out cellular respiration, day and night

objetivos.leitura: Alleles are versions of the same gene. A homozygous individual has two identical alleles (AA or aa); a heterozygous individual has two different alleles (Aa). The dominant allele is expressed with just one copy; the recessive allele is expressed only in two copies. In the Aa x Aa cross, the expected ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa, that is, 3 with the dominant trait for every 1 with the recessive trait.

etapas.entra: each passes on A or a
one copy of the dominant allele is enough

objetivos.vida_real: Each parent has two cards, one A and one a, and passes one on at random. In four rounds, you would expect to get AA once, Aa twice, and aa once. But, as with any random draw, the results can differ with only a few rounds.
pegadinhas: A 3-to-1 ratio is expected, not guaranteed with only a few offspring.
Aa shows the dominant trait, even though it carries the recessive allele.

questoes.pergunta: Which of these individuals is heterozygous?
questoes.trecho: A heterozygous individual has two different alleles (Aa)

questoes.pergunta: In the Aa x Aa cross, what is the expected phenotype ratio?
questoes.explicacao: 1 : 2 : 1 is the genotype ratio; the phenotype ratio is 3 : 1.
questoes.trecho: the phenotype ratio is 3 dominant to 1 recessive

questoes.pergunta: When is the recessive allele expressed?
questoes.explicacao: When an A is present, the dominant trait is expressed.
questoes.trecho: The recessive allele is expressed only with two copies (aa)
